scope: Local regression and component measurements, production-configuration Docker build tests, and loopback browser comparison. No live-site traffic or timing result.

protocol.rationale: TLS1.3 permits a zero-length ticket nonce and requires distinct nonces for tickets on the same connection. The nonce is the HKDF resumption context.
protocol.encoding: Counter 0 is empty; positive counters use shortest unsigned big-endian encoding. This mapping is injective.
protocol.keyDerivation: The same nonce bytes and length are serialized and passed to HKDF. PSK values change consistently with the new context.
protocol.entropy: The nonce remains a public counter. Random ticket generation, 32-byte stateful identity and resumption-master-secret entropy are unchanged.
protocol.exhaustion: UINT64_MAX is reserved. A TLS1.3 fatal error precedes ticket/session construction at that value, preventing counter wrap and repeated construction retries.

regression.assertions: Minimal distinct nonce encodings, distinct per-ticket PSKs, matching client/server PSKs and actual resumption from every captured counter-suite ticket. Parser cases include legal 255-byte nonce and malformed/truncated/empty-ticket/trailing-body rejection.
regression.parserScope: Direct internal packet-parser fixtures; not malformed encrypted network traffic.

negativeControl.scope: Exact final harness linked to otherwise identical combined library with only statem_srvr.c restored to pinned upstream source.
negativeControl.failure: First-ticket 8-byte nonce fails canonical empty encoding assertion.

componentMeasurement.scope: Complete first NewSessionTicket handshake message, including handshake header; excludes TLS record wrappers, TCP/IP, DNS and document body.
componentMeasurement.control: Same combined source and headers; only statem_srvr.c restored to pinned upstream source.

nativeBrowsers.scope: macOS arm64; Playwright 1.63.0; loopback TLS1.3 HTTP/1.1, Connection:close, one stateful ticket; ephemeral in-memory certificate/key; no system trust changes.

chromium.finding: Empty-nonce ticket parsing and PSK-based resumption observed.

webkit.finding: Document delivery succeeds with both variants; ticket-resumption compatibility remains unestablished.

limitations: One OpenSSL version and one native version per browser engine; not universal client compatibility.
The 8-byte component reduction does not establish complete-exchange delivery-overhead savings or browser speed improvements.
Production activation and live measurements are separate evidence.
